the DDC transistor can be implemented on bulk CMO S, can be fabricated with existing technology, and can reduce power by 50 percent.

(1) the DDC transistor provides a low-cost solution to re-enable supply-voltage scaling by reducing random variability, providing a strong body effect and compensating for environmental effects; and (2) the DDC technology can be used to reduce power consumption of a variety of circuits by 50 percent at matched performance.

the deeply depleted channel transistor can be implemented on both legacy and future CMOS processes and provides a low-cost solution to re-enable transistor threshold voltage scaling, which in turn enables a 50 percent reduction in power consumption at matched performance.

the reduction of transistor variability and the development of new devices that will enable the continued scaling of CMOS devices.
the design of novel transistors that can enable low voltage and low power operation for future generations of CMOS circuits.
the reduction of transistor variability in order to reduce power consumption of high performance CMOS circuits.

the deeply-depleted channel (DDC) transistor is a very attractive option for low-power and high-performance CMOS ICs.
the deeply-depleted channel FET (DDC FET) is a low cost solution that can be used to reduce variability and enable voltage scaling on both legacy and future CMOS fabrication processes.
the deeply depleted channel transistor is the best option to re-enable transistor-threshold voltage reduction for high performance low power CMOS integrated circuits.

the DDC is an excellent candidate for future CMOS scaling.
we have demonstrated the viability and benefits of the deep depleted channel transistor on both future and mature CMOS fabrication processes.

we have developed a new transistor structure that is compatible with existing CMOS fabrication processes that has a lower variability and therefore allows us to scale the supply voltage to lower power consumption.
the DDC transistor can provide a strong body effect and reduce variability in a bulk CMOS process, enabling a return to aggressive voltage scaling.
the deeply depleted channel transistor provides a low-cost solution to reduce random variability and enable voltage scaling.
